steps.title: Declare the parameters
notes: Every parameter you see in the profile dialog is created here, once, when the project is compiled. create_top_level_group makes the group, the add_* calls add one parameter each: id, minimum, maximum, default, unit.

FLAGS.OPT_OFF makes the group optional and switched off: that is the off you switch to on in the video. The hatch group at the end gives the downskin its own hatching with a finer hatch distance (0.08 mm).

lines: // Off by default. surface_angle (degrees): regions whose surface is
// flatter than this angle are downskin (0 = horizontal overhang).
// reference_layers: number of layers below that are compared (max. 20,
// min_width (mm): narrower downskin slivers are ignored.
// overlap (mm): the downskin hatch reaches this far into the volume.
// *_splitting: contours inside the downskin get the downskin BSIDs.
// MPBF background: downskin hatch uses a smaller hatch distance (0.08 mm)
// and, via its BSID, lower power: above powder the heat cannot flow
// away, so less energy is needed to avoid sagging and rough surfaces.

steps.title: Read the values from the profile
notes: Before the layers are calculated, the values of the part's profile are copied into a plain JavaScript object. From here on the code never talks to the UI again: it only uses part.overhang.surface_angle, part.overhang.reference_layers and so on.
enabled is the group's on/off switch. Move the angle slider in Try it: this is the value that ends up in surface_angle.

steps.title: Find the downskin of every island
notes: The exposure of a layer is calculated island by island (an island is one closed area of a part in a layer). For each island the code asks for its downskin area, but only if the group is enabled; otherwise the area stays empty and nothing below changes.
Downskin has priority: where an area is both downskin and upskin (a thin plate), the upskin is cut away.

lines: // Skin areas: downskin has priority over upskin.
// MPBF background: downskin = area whose surface is flatter than the
// 'surface angle' compared with the reference layers below (powder
// below); upskin = area not covered by the next layer above (top
// surface). Slivers narrower than 'min width' are dropped, because
// they would only create very short vectors.
let l_ds = l_part.overhang.enabled ? SKIN.split_downskin(a_ctx.model, a_island, l_part.overhang) : ISL.empty();
let l_us = l_part.upskin.enabled ? SKIN.split_upskin_one_layer(a_island, l_part.upskin) : ISL.empty();

steps.title: Compare with the layers below
notes: The real work is done by the ATU builtin splitMultiLayerOverhangExt2. It compares the island with iRefLayers layers below and returns the part that is flatter than fMaxSurfaceAngle: the layers on the left stop at the first shelf layer, the blue part has no support below.
bUseSolidSupportsBelow: areas that rest on solid supports are not downskin. Finally ISL.opening removes slivers narrower than min_width.

lines: // Only these option keys are used on purpose (unknown keys raise an error).
// fOverlap 0: the overlap into the volume is added later by the caller
//   (overhang.overlap in exposure_layer.js), only for the hatch area.
// bIncreaseAccuracy: extra processing for a more accurate result
// bUseSolidSupportsBelow: solid supports in the layers below are taken
//   into account, so areas resting on solid supports are not treated
// bEnableSharpCorners: less rounded corners in the result.
// volumeResult (the non-overhang part) is filled but not used here.
// The opening result is clipped to the island, so the downskin never
// reaches outside of the part outline.

steps.title: Grow into the volume and hatch
notes: The downskin area is grown by overlap (light blue on the left, exaggerated) and cut out of the volume, so the downskin hatch and the volume hatch overlap a little and bond.
Then every area is hatched with its own settings and its own vector type: the volume with BSID 500, the downskin with BSID.hatch_downskin (501).

lines: // The skin areas are grown by their 'overlap' (mm) before they are
// clipped to the hatch area. The skin hatch then reaches a little into
// the neighboring volume, which bonds both areas and avoids a gap at
hatch_area(a_ctx, a_result, l_split.hull, l_part.hatching.volume, BSID.hatch_volume, l_id, l_b, false);
hatch_area(a_ctx, a_result, l_ds_area, l_part.overhang.hatch, BSID.hatch_downskin, l_id, l_b, false);

steps.title: Less energy for BSID 501
notes: The vector type table gives every BSID its default laser power, speed, scan order and preview colour. The downskin variants are their normal type + 1, with less power: 120 W instead of 280 W for the hatch.
These are only defaults: they fill the Scanning group, where you can change them per profile without touching the code. The colour is the blue you see in the Exposure Preview.

lines: //          key                    bsid family               ds     P[W] v[mm/s] order color

recipes.title: Switch downskin on by default
recipes.why: New profiles start with downskin detection enabled.
recipes.result: In a new profile, “Multi-layer overhang (downskin)” shows on. Profiles you already have may keep their stored setting.

recipes.title: Use 30° as the default surface angle
recipes.why: Only clearly flat overhangs become downskin; the 30° slope of the demo part would then be self-supporting.
recipes.result: The default changes to 30°. Set the slider in Try it to 30° to preview what this does to the demo part. For a single profile you do not need code: just change the value in the dialog.

recipes.title: Lower the default downskin hatch power
recipes.why: Less energy above the powder, e.g. for a material that sags easily.
recipes.result: Downskin hatch default 100 W: about 42 J/mm³ instead of 50 J/mm³ (100 / (1000 · 0.08 · 0.03)). For one profile, change Scanning › Downskin hatching › power in the dialog instead.

recipes.title: Show downskin in another colour
recipes.why: A colour that stands out better in your screenshots. Only the preview changes, not the toolpath.
recipes.result: The downskin hatch is drawn purple in the Exposure Preview and the 3D View.

recipes.title: Allow more than 20 reference layers
recipes.why: Very thin layers need more layers below to recognise a flat overhang. The limit lives in two places that must match.
recipes.result: Reference layers accepts up to 40. lower_layers_dependence tells ATU how many layers below a layer depends on; if it is smaller than the parameter, the single-layer preview can show a different downskin than the full build.
